amendments.rule: **Hebrew has no verb *to have*, so an English *have* is a recasting and belongs to whatever made the clause possessive.** Where `הָיָה` is present it is the existential and takes the *have* itself, its preposition goes `unrepresented` under rule 40, and the suffix takes the subject pronoun: `וַיְהִי לוֹ נָשִׁים` → *he had* … *wives* puts *had* on `הָיָה` and *he* on the suffix. Where the clause is verbless, the possessive preposition is what makes it possessive and carries the *have*: `לָהֶם מִסְגְּרוֹת` → *they had panels* puts *had* on `לְ` and *they* on the suffix, and `שָׁפְרָה עָלָי` → *I have a goodly heritage* puts *have* on `עַל` and *I* on the suffix. Where neither is present, a possessive suffix can be the possession by itself and takes the supplied verb with its pronoun: `טוֹבָתִי בַּל עָלֶיךָ` → *I have no good beyond thee* gives the suffix *I have*, headed on the pronoun. Another finite verb in the clause does not qualify merely by being finite. `שָׁפְרָה` is not a copula: the ASV renders it by the attributive *goodly*, which is its lexeme, so the *have* is not its. **But a verb the ASV has itself rendered by the *have* does qualify, and the same subtraction decides it.** Where the Hebrew writes a verb of falling or allotment and the English writes *have* in its place — `יִפְּלוּ בְנַחֲלָה` → *they shall have inheritance* — dropping the word leaves that verb with no rendering at all, so the *have* is the verb's own together with the subject pronoun rule 17 keeps there, and a preposition beside it whose relation the ASV has left unstated goes `unrepresented` under rule 40. **And where nothing in the clause makes it possessive, the word is not to be placed at all.** A clause that writes no `הָיָה`, no possessive preposition, no suffix and no verb the *have* renders has no morpheme to carry it: `יוֹסֵף חֲבָלִים` → *Joseph* ***shall have two*** *portions* leaves the supplied verb its own `added` unit under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause, together with any numeral, subject or object the ASV supplies alongside it, while the possessed noun keeps only its own word. Do not fold such a word into that noun, into a neighbouring clause's verb, or into a preposition standing elsewhere in the verse to avoid the `added`, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*: it is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. Test by subtraction, as in rule 16 — drop the *have* and ask which morpheme has lost its rendering. If only the possession relation is gone, the *have* is the preposition's or the suffix's; if a written verb is left with nothing, it is that verb's; and if nothing in the clause is diminished but a possession the English has supplied, it is `added`. **Read *no possessive preposition* and *no suffix* in that count as none the ASV has left an English word for.** A preposition or a suffix on which the ASV has already spent its own word stands in the same position as an absent one: it is not what makes the clause possessive, and it is not a home for a second English word, exactly as rule 52 counts a preposition's function words against the morphemes that could carry them and rule 51 says a waw holding an English word of its own is not a home for a second one. What this rule's earlier sentences govern is a `בְּ` or a `לְ` that is itself the clause's predicate, for which the ASV writes no preposition at all — `אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ מוּם` → *that hath a blemish* — and not a locative or other phrase the ASV has rendered in full. `אוֹ תְבַלֻּל בְּעֵינוֹ` → *or* ***that hath*** *a blemish in his eye* writes *in* for the `בְּ`, *his* for the suffix, *eye* for the noun and *a blemish* for `תְּבַלֻּל`, so nothing is left for the *hath* to complete and it is its own `added` unit; `מְרוֹחַ אָשֶׁךְ` → ***hath his*** *stones broken* goes the same way, the adjective keeping *broken* and the noun *stones*, with the supplied *his* `added` besides under rule 18's closing sentence. Count the clause's English words against the morphemes that could carry them before reaching for one that is already spent. **And where the possessive clause is a relative clause, the written relative supplies the English subject and the resumptive suffix takes nothing.** `אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ מוּם` → *that hath a blemish* gives *that* to `אֲשֶׁר` and *hath* to the `בְּ`, and the suffix is `unrepresented` under rule 22, since two morphemes point at the antecedent and the ASV writes one word for it; the same clause written without a relative gives the suffix the subject pronoun this rule's earlier sentences direct, as `מוּם בּוֹ` → *he hath a blemish* does. A written `הָיָה` in such a clause still takes the *have* itself and leaves both the preposition and the suffix `unrepresented`: `אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בּוֹ מוּם` → *that hath a blemish*. **And an interrogative particle standing in such a clause does not take the *have* either.** Where `הֲ`, or the `אִם` opening a disjunctive question, stands in a possessive clause and the ASV marks the question by fronting the possessive verb itself, that word is the possessive morpheme's under this rule's earlier sentences and the particle is `unrepresented` under rule 17's sentence on a question marked by inversion alone: `וְאִם־זְרוֹעַ כָּאֵל לָךְ` → *Or* ***hast*** *thou an arm like God* gives *hast* to the `לְ` and *thou* to its suffix, and leaves the `אִם` nothing. Rule 20's fronted-copula sentence and rule 50's reading of an interrogative existential clause reach a copula the construction supplies and an existential frame, which are words no other morpheme licenses; a *have* is neither, since this rule assigns it to the `הָיָה`, the preposition, the suffix or the verb that makes the clause possessive, and handing it to the particle would leave that morpheme holding nothing while the relation it alone carries went unrendered, against rule 2. Read what the fronted word is rather than that the clause is a question: where the ASV writes a separate question auxiliary besides the *have* — a *Do*, a *Shall* or a *Will* at the clause head — that word is the particle's under rule 17 as before, and the *have* still goes where this rule sends it.
amendments.why: JOB.40.9 `וְאִם־זְרוֹעַ כָּאֵל לָךְ` → *Or hast thou an arm like God* is a possessive verbless clause opening with an interrogative particle, and the contract gave no ruling on it: rule 43 says an English *have* belongs to the morpheme that makes the clause possessive, while rules 20 and 50 hand a fronted finite word in an interrogative verbless clause to the particle. The verse pass read the collision the second way and left the `לְ` — the one morpheme carrying the possession — with no English at all, which rule 2 forbids and rule 43's own subtraction test contradicts. The gap is in rule 43, which never mentions interrogatives, so the qualification belongs there rather than in a new rule pointing back at it. Rules 20 and 50 are not touched: their own sentences already name a construction-supplied copula (*Is*, *Am*, *Art*, *Are*, *Was*) and an existential frame, and neither list reaches a *have*; rule 17 already provides the inversion-only case this amendment invokes. The corpus tables supplied for this chapter cover none of these lemmas and so contradict nothing; rule 43's own cited precedents (`לָהֶם מִסְגְּרוֹת` → *they had panels*, `שָׁפְרָה עָלָי` → *I have a goodly heritage*) are the evidence, and the construction recurs wherever Hebrew asks a possessive question.

conventions: A fronted English question word goes to a present הֲ or אִם where it is an auxiliary the clause would not otherwise write — *Shall* at v2, the distributed *Wilt ... Wilt* at v8 — but not where it is the lexical word another morpheme licenses: the *hast* of v9 is the possessive לְ's under rule 43, and the particle is `unrepresented` under rule 17, the question being marked by inversion alone. Where no interrogative morpheme stands, the fronted auxiliary is the verb's own: *Shall any take* at v24 and *canst thou thunder* in v9's second clause.

A preposition the ASV supplies between a verb and a following bare nominal goes to the verb under rule 44 wherever that nominal or suffix is the verb's own object — *argueth with* (v2), *demand of* and *declare unto* (v7), *Deck ... with* and *array ... with* (v10), *look upon* (v11), *Look on* (v12), *confess of* (v14) — and to the noun under rule 33 only where the verb already carries its object, as at v22, where the object suffix on יְסֻכֻּהוּ leaves צִלֲלוֹ an adjunct and the *with* the noun's own. Two identical constructions in one verse are not to be divided between the two rules; v10 was corrected on that ground.

The entreaty particle נָא is rendered by a bare *now* throughout this chapter (vv. 7, 10, 15, 16) and takes that word as its own aligned unit headed on it. Rule 30's *I beseech thee* formula is not written here, so nothing of it is to be supplied, and the particle is neither `unrepresented` nor fused into the imperative or presentative standing beside it.

Where the ASV recasts a clause with a locative relative *where*, this chapter gives the word to the locative morpheme rather than to a connective or to nothing: תַּחְתָּם takes *where ... stand* at v12, its suffix taking *they*, and שָׁם takes *Where* at v20, the waw of that clause being left `unrepresented`. Rule 17's waw-to-*which* recasting is the competing reading at v20 and is named in that unit.

report: Cross-verse check: all 18 candidate groups resolve to ASV wording or a source-licensed difference, not to a split. The waw buckets (Moreover/Then/and/Yea/but/Or/And) are read off the ASV as rule 14 directs; הִנֵּה Behold (v15) vs Lo (v16) is wording; רָאָה look upon (v11) vs Look on (v12) is one construction handled one way under rule 44; כֹּל + גֵּאֶה is identical in vv.11-12; the הַ buckets differ only by whether the ASV wrote a *the*; תַּחַת differs by whether a suffix stands on it; the remaining lemmas are one-occurrence contexts with distinct ASV renderings.

The candidate table is blind to `added` units, so I read the dump for the fold-vs-add split it cannot see. The six additions are supplied connectives and pronouns with no licensing morpheme — *and* (v12), *only* and the indirect *him* (v19), *if* (v23), *Or* and *his* (v24) — and every supplied word folded into a unit instead has a morpheme that licenses it: *place* completes the substantival participle at v13 (rule 31), *as* states the predicate nominal's own relation at v18 (rule 33), and the supplied *the*s and *a*s go to the nominals they determine (rule 15). Nothing is added in one verse and folded in another.

Supplied prepositions after verbs are the chapter's most repeated judgment and are consistent: the verb takes the word wherever the Hebrew noun or suffix is its own object (vv. 2, 7 twice, 10 twice, 11, 12, 14), and only v22 gives it to the noun under rule 33, where the object suffix on יְסֻכֻּהוּ already carries the verb's object and צִלֲלוֹ is an adjunct. v10's review note records that it was corrected onto rule 44 for exactly that reason.

One genuine error, patched at JOB.40.9. The verse gave the fronted *hast* to the interrogative אִם and left the possessive לְ of לָךְ unrepresented. Rule 43 is categorical that an English *have* is a recasting belonging to whatever made the clause possessive, and its subtraction test finds only the possession relation gone when *hast* is dropped; rule 20's fronted-copula sentence names *Is/Am/Art/Are/Was* and rule 50's names an existential frame, and neither reaches a *have*. *hast* now goes to לָ, *thou* to its suffix, and אִם is `unrepresented` under rule 17's inversion-only sentence. The second clause of the same verse writes no particle and keeps *canst thou* with תַרְעֵם as before.

BSB: six disagreements, five of them documented convention differences rather than errors — אֶת at vv.1 and 6 (rule 16, the object written bare), לְ at v14 and v20 (rule 40 recastings: a bare English object *thee* and a bare indirect object *him*), and the waw at v20, which is the Where/שָׁם judgment the verse pass named as contested. The sixth, לְ at v9, is the genuine error above; it was corrected on rule 43's grounds, not to move the agreement rate, and the rate is not a target.

Also checked and left standing: v8's distributed *Wilt ... Wilt* on one הֲ (rule 25's interrogative sentence), v12's *where they stand* and v20's *Where* both on the locative morpheme, v16 and v18's copulas on their prepositional predicates (rule 49) against v18 and v19's copulas on their nominal predicates (rule 20), and the four נָא units all rendered by a bare *now*. Four conventions recorded; one amendment to rule 43.
